I am 64, been farming this 6 mu in Quzhou for 40 years. Wheat-maize rotation, same as everyone around here. My son is grown and gone, just me working the land, but the well water is reliable and I hire the combine at harvest time.

Last year wheat gave me about 480 kg/mu, maize about 580 kg/mu. That is normal for our village. I will do similar this year — no reason to change what works.

For wheat (winter), I plant in early October. I use improved seed from the agro-shop, the Jimai variety most neighbors plant. I put down compound fertilizer (15-15-15) at sowing, about 50 kg/mu — that gives me roughly 7.5 kg N, P, and K. Then I topdress with urea around jointing in March, about 25 kg/mu (that's about 11.5 kg N). So total nitrogen comes to around 19 kg/mu. I irrigate three times — before winter, at jointing, and at grain filling. I spray once for aphids and powdery mildew, sometimes twice if the weather is wet.

For maize (summer), I plant right after wheat harvest in mid-June, no tilling, just direct seed into the stubble. Hybrid seed, Zhengdan or similar. I apply compound fertilizer with the seeder, about 40 kg/mu, then topdress urea at the big trumpet stage, about 30 kg/mu. Total N around 20 kg/mu. Maize here needs less irrigation because of summer rain — usually 2 times if the rain is enough. One spray for borer and armyworm.

I do not want to cut fertilizer. If I save 50 yuan and lose 50 kg of grain, that is a bad trade. Better to put on enough.
